closure_evidence.closure_notes: Review does not pass. dvmChangeStatus at Thread.cpp:2905 reads the old status and returns it when the new status is the same. THREAD_RUNNING is stored first with android_atomic_acquire_store, then suspendCount is observed; a nonzero count calls fullSuspendCheck. fullSuspendCheck locks gDvm.threadSuspendCountLock through dvmLockMutex, stores THREAD_SUSPENDED, and waits in dvmWaitCond until suspendCount is zero. That wait is pthread_cond_wait on gDvm.threadSuspendCountCond and stops at Bionic.PthreadCondition. The paired pthread_mutex_lock and pthread_mutex_unlock are required symbols of that same owner and are not a second cluster. After the wait, dbgSuspendCount is asserted zero, the previous status is restored, and the lock is released. A non-RUNNING request, including THREAD_WAIT and THREAD_TIMED_WAIT, uses android_atomic_release_store and asserts the request is not THREAD_SUSPENDED. It does not touch waitCond or waitMutex. Those fields are initialized at Thread.cpp:939 and the wait, interrupt, and signal protocol is in Sync.cpp, which this path does not call. dvmThreadStartup initializes the suspend lock and condition before any transition. ScopedJniThreadState around RegisterNatives only performs the RUNNING enter and THREAD_NATIVE exit. The cutils acquire and release stores are the status-word barriers inside this owner. This REOPEN_REQUIRED crossing blocks SOURCE_CLOSED.

internal_deps: pthread_cond_t is one volatile int; bit 0 is COND_SHARED_MASK and the other bits are a counter stepped by 2
pthread_cond_init stores 0, then sets bit 0 only when the attribute is PTHREAD_PROCESS_SHARED (1); PTHREAD_PROCESS_PRIVATE is 0
pthread_cond_destroy stores 0xdeadc04d and does not wake waiters; the wait path does not test that sentinel
pthread_cond_wait calls pthread_cond_timedwait with a NULL abstime, which waits without a timeout
pthread_cond_timedwait samples CLOCK_REALTIME; pthread_cond_timedwait_monotonic and pthread_cond_timedwait_monotonic_np sample CLOCK_MONOTONIC
an absolute deadline that is already past returns ETIMEDOUT before the mutex is unlocked
otherwise __timespec_to_absolute subtracts the sampled clock and borrows one second when tv_nsec is negative, then the relative wait uses that timespec
pthread_cond_timedwait_relative_np and pthread_cond_timeout_np do not call clock_gettime; timeout_np builds seconds and nanoseconds from the millisecond argument
__pthread_cond_timedwait_relative samples cond->value, unlocks the mutex, waits, then locks the mutex again and ignores both mutex return values
only a futex status of -ETIMEDOUT is returned as ETIMEDOUT; every other futex status, including a compare mismatch or an interruption, returns 0
signal and broadcast share __pthread_cond_pulse; signal passes 1 and broadcast passes INT_MAX
pulse keeps the shared bit, subtracts 2 from the counter with __bionic_cmpxchg until it succeeds, runs ANDROID_MEMBAR_FULL, then wakes
a normal mutex uses bits 1-0 for unlocked 0, locked 1, and contended 2; bit 13 is the shared flag; bits 15-14 are the type
normal unlock decrements and wakes one waiter only from the contended state; the wait comment says a mismatched futex value returns immediately
__futex_wait_ex and __futex_wake_ex use FUTEX_WAIT or FUTEX_WAKE when pshared is nonzero, and OR FUTEX_PRIVATE_FLAG 128 otherwise
linux/futex.h defines FUTEX_WAIT as 0 and FUTEX_WAKE as 1 and does not define FUTEX_PRIVATE_FLAG, so the 128 fallback in bionic_futex.h is the value used
the x86 and ARM stubs return the raw syscall register and do not call __set_errno; ARM __futex_syscall4 branches to __futex_syscall3 with the four arguments already in r0-r3
pthread_mutex_lock_timeout_np samples CLOCK_MONOTONIC through the same timespec helpers and is not on the condition-wait return path

internal_deps: both wrappers pass the caller's clock id and timespec pointer through to the syscall and do not branch on the id
x86 loads the id into ebx and the pointer into ecx, then uses int $0x80 with __NR_clock_gettime
ARM EABI leaves the id in r0 and the pointer in r1, saves r7, and uses swi #0
a syscall result outside [-MAX_ERRNO, -1] is returned unchanged
a result inside that range is negated and passed to __set_errno, which stores errno and returns -1
x86 then forces eax to -1; ARM returns the value from __set_errno
CLOCK_REALTIME is 0 and CLOCK_MONOTONIC is 1; pthread_cond_timedwait passes the former and the monotonic timed waits pass the latter
an unrecognized clock id is not checked in the wrapper
time_t is __kernel_time_t, typedef long in the x86 32-bit and ARM posix type headers, and timespec is tv_sec plus long tv_nsec

Linux clock_gettime kernel boundary.request_schema: 32-bit clock_gettime syscall number, the caller's clock id unchanged, and a pointer to a timespec of time_t tv_sec plus long tv_nsec
Linux clock_gettime kernel boundary.response_schema: kernel writes tv_sec and tv_nsec and returns 0, or returns a negative errno and does not complete a successful sample
Linux clock_gettime kernel boundary.lifecycle: one int $0x80 on x86 or one swi #0 on ARM; the wrapper does not retry
Linux clock_gettime kernel boundary.error_semantics: kernel failure is a return in [-MAX_ERRNO, -1]; MAX_ERRNO is 4095

closure_evidence.closure_notes: The x86 and ARM stubs are the gensyscalls.py templates. They do not interpret clock ids or timespec fields. __set_errno stores the positive errno and returns -1, so both architectures have the same libc return on the error path. The Linux syscall instruction is the excluded kernel boundary. Bionic's errno store and -1 return stay in this owner and are not part of that boundary. pthread_cond_timedwait's choice of CLOCK_REALTIME or CLOCK_MONOTONIC is the caller's argument, already recorded on Bionic.PthreadCondition. This source record does not review Runtime/NativeCore/agr_runtime.c.
